evidence.quote: Vestas continued to navigate significant challenges arising from shifting geopolitical tensions across the world.
Project execution at Vestas involves delivering complex onshore and offshore projects within specified parameters relating to quality, cost, and timeline.
Vestas’ digital and other critical assets are exposed to cyber attacks. A cyber attack may have dual implications for both Vestas as a company and for the societies that our energy solutions serve.
The GHG emissions from Vestas’ own operations and value chain have a negative impact on the global climate and environment.
High carbon taxes and tariffs increase the price of GHG intense materials such as steel, increasing the overall cost to produce wind turbines.
The GHG emissions originating in our supply chain from the extraction, production and transportation of raw materials and products have a negative impact on biodiversity and ecosystems

title: Non-recyclable Materials
section: E5 Circular economy and resource use

evidence.quote: Non-recyclable materials in turbines might be landfilled or incinerated and increase the need for virgin materials, which has a negative impact on the environment.
The negative impact related to health and safety incidents.
Potential injuries leading to delays, lost work hours and compensation costs pose a financial risk.

title: Health and Safety Incidents
section: S2 Workers in the value chain

evidence.quote: Potential injuries to value chain workers leading to delays, lost work hours and compensation costs pose a risk.

title: Child and Forced Labour
section: S2 Workers in the value chain

evidence.quote: Risk of forced and child labour in our supply chain.
Vestas’ global network of suppliers combined with the risk of fines related to child and forced labour constitute a potential risk.
Land-use restrictions during wind farm construction leading to a temporary negative impact in the form of physical and economic displacement (e.g income losses) of local communities.
Inadequate grid expansion, ineffective auction design and permit delays could increase costs, hinder investments, and reduce the viability of wind deployment.
Vestas’ global presence presents an increased risk of exposure to corruption and bribery.

Energy is consumed during the manufacture of wind turbine components and the construction and servicing of wind parks. Energy consumption in our own operations relies on fossil fuels, leading to resource depletion and emissions that negatively impact the climate.
